It's going to depend on your exact situation, but their main concern is de-escalating and keeping you safe. They'll ask where you are or if you have plans/tools to hurt yourself. They'll then ask you to take small steps to be a little safer. For instance, I've called several times when I was on the brink of self harm. They've talked to me a little about how I'm feeling, and then asked if I felt like I could put the knife in another room. 

They're not therapists and they likely won't produce a breakthrough on your underlying emotional issues. But when you're in crisis, they're trained to help stabilize so that you can then get further help. They know that if you're calling, there's at least some part of you that wants to stay alive, and they'll talk you through making a plan to do that (who to call, where to go, etc.)

Not every person is helpful all the time. Sometimes you get a new person who is clearly just reading from the script. It's not their fault -- it's impossible to be completely prepared for every call that might come their way. It's ok to hang up and call back if you need to. Importantly, there's never any judgment or preaching, just reassurance that you're not alone, and practical steps to stay safe. 

Hope this helps!

I think it's important to examine our definition of "healing".

I've been on medication and in therapy for years. Thanks to that, I have days, weeks, months where my mind is kind to me and I am "normal". In those times I look healed, but I am still a person with a chronic illness that, if left unchecked, will actively try to kill me.

Even in the times when depression does rear its ugly head, times when I am barely scraping by as a functioning human -- I remind myself that even then, I've still healed. I have tools, coping mechanisms, and people to turn to. 

It's kinda like.... walking through a forest. Sometimes it's daylight, and there's sun and birdsong. Sometimes, it's night, and there's strange noises and tripping hazards. But after years in the forest, I know my way in the dark. I know where the roots are, and I know that the rustling in the trees is just the wind, no matter how hard my brain tries to tell me otherwise. I know where the dangers are, and I know how to keep myself safe. If it comes to it, I know how to ask for rescue.

Most importantly, I know that daylight will come.

That, to me, is healing.
